findings.text: follow-on: the barrier waits for the supervisor's own log prose 'unknown request: standby-ready-probe', so a reworded log line in fleet_supervisor.handle_line would make the wait time out and the test fail for a reason unrelated to lease behaviour; readiness is signalled by log text rather than by a protocol.
follow-on: _wait_for and _request still duplicate the helpers in tests/test_fleet_supervisor_standby.py:15-30, so a change to the supervisor request protocol must be made in two files.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit 7ebe719f against base 4c6d6126: one file, +17/-8, adding a request-response barrier and redirecting supervisor stdout to a log the barrier reads.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when's four-file gate is unchanged; the reviewed manifest records it as 16 passed EXIT=0 in barrier-committed-head-gate.log, and the same command reproduced 16 passed EXIT=0 in this review.
item_verdicts.goal: the delta strengthens the pre-promotion half of the node goal (a standby claims no declared-service lease until promotion) by reading the supervisor's own read-loop log line before asserting lease.holder() is None.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; baseline_suite and after_suite are now populated (base 01406cea and head 7ebe719f, both exit 0 with no failures), which lets the added-failure count be measured; the prior review found baseline_suite empty.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the gained commit touches only tests/test_standby_promotion_claims_leases.py, one of the manifest's three declared write paths.

justifications.durability: the barrier closes the exact race the prior review named and the negative-control pair demonstrates the guard fires; residual: the readiness signal is a log string, and the assertion is a one-shot check taken after the barrier.
justifications.evidence: this review re-ran the four-file gate at 7ebe719f: 16 passed EXIT=0; the run's own logs show the old test passing the startup-reload mutation (1 passed, EXIT=0) while the revised test fails it (1 failed, EXIT=1), and this review reproduced that pair independently; baseline_suite and after_suite are both populated so added_failure_count is measured as 0, though the after_suite arm is single-file rather than the four-file gate.
justifications.fit: the barrier follows the file's existing _wait_for idiom, but couples the test to the exact log prose 'unknown request: ...' and still duplicates the sibling test's _wait_for and _request.
justifications.goal_fidelity: tests/test_standby_promotion_claims_leases.py:62-67 now waits for the supervisor's read loop (the 'unknown request: standby-ready-probe' line logged by fleet_supervisor.handle_line) before line 68 asserts no lease holder, so the pre-promotion assertion measures a settled standby rather than a startup race.
justifications.reuse: the test drives the existing reckon/crew/host_lease.py:HostLease.claim and reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:serve with no parallel mechanism, at the cost of re-implementing readiness by log scraping rather than a shared request-and-ack helper.
justifications.scope_discipline: the gained commit changes only tests/test_standby_promotion_claims_leases.py, within the manifest's declared write paths, and names no plan, sprint or ticket identifier.
